items.stem: Why does a computer need an operating system?
options: To provide an interface between the user/applications and the hardware and to manage resources
To translate programs into machine code
To stop the computer being hacked
items.answer: To provide an interface between the user/applications and the hardware and to manage resources
items.markingKey: OS: manages hardware, memory, files, processes and security; provides a user interface and platform for applications.

items.stem: Describe two tasks carried out by the file management function of an operating system.
items.answer: Organises files in a directory/folder structure; controls naming, creation, deletion, copying, moving; manages access rights to files; allocates storage space on disk.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per task, max 2 [2]

items.stem: Explain why a network technician might prefer a command-line interface to a GUI.
items.answer: Commands can be combined and scripted to automate tasks; direct access to settings; uses fewer resources; works remotely over slow links.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per point, max 2 [2]

items.stem: Yusuf uses a laptop at Summit Engineering to run a web browser, a spreadsheet and a music player at the same time. Explain how the OS enables the new printer to be used.
items.answer: Hardware management installs/loads the device driver, which translates OS commands into printer commands; manages the print queue/buffer.
items.markingKey: 1 mark driver; 1 mark explanation [2]

items.stem: A new printer is connected to the computer of Chloe. (a) State two features of the GUI that help a new user. (b) Explain why the OS must handle interrupts.
items.answer: (a) Icons, menus, windows, pointer, help screens, drag and drop. (b) Devices and programs signal events; OS responds by running ISRs and scheduling, ensuring urgent events are dealt with.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Pioneer Insurance in Lagos is installing an operating system on 50 new office computers. (a) Explain how the OS enables the new printer to be used. (b) Describe how the OS keeps each user's files private.
items.answer: (a) Hardware management installs/loads the device driver, which translates OS commands into printer commands; manages the print queue/buffer. (b) User accounts with passwords; access rights/permissions for files and folders.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark driver; 1 mark explanation [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: The IT team at Palm Grove Hotel is writing a policy on computer use. Discuss whether a GUI or a command-line interface is more suitable for the staff at Palm Grove Hotel.
items.answer: Points in favour: GUI: intuitive, little training, visual, suitable for most office staff; CLI: fast for experts, scriptable, low resources, remote use. Points against / limitations: GUI uses more memory/processing and hides advanced options; CLI needs commands to be learned and errors are easy to make. Conclusion: GUI for general staff, CLI for technical administrators.

items.stem: Explain how the operating system allows several programs to appear to run at the same time on one processor core.
items.answer: Process management/scheduling gives each process a short time slice in turn; interrupts switch between them; this happens so fast that they appear simultaneous.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: time slices/scheduling; 1 mark: rapid switching via interrupts [2]

items.stem: Describe the role of memory management.
items.answer: Allocates memory to processes and frees it when they end; prevents one process using another's memory (protection); manages virtual memory/paging when RAM is full.

items.stem: What does a disk defragmenter do?
options: Deletes all files on a disk
Rearranges the parts of files on a hard disk so each file is stored in contiguous blocks
items.answer: Rearranges the parts of files on a hard disk so each file is stored in contiguous blocks
items.markingKey: Defragmentation reduces read-head movement, speeding up file access on HDDs.

items.stem: Explain why defragmenting a hard disk drive can improve performance.
items.answer: Fragmented files are spread across the disk so the read head must move many times; after defragmentation each file is in contiguous sectors, so fewer head movements and faster access.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: fragments scattered; 1 mark: head movement/seek time reduced; 1 mark: faster access [3]

items.stem: The IT team at Atlas Museum is writing a policy on computer use. Discuss whether a GUI or a command-line interface is more suitable for the staff at Atlas Museum.
items.answer: Points in favour: GUI: intuitive, little training, visual, suitable for most office staff; CLI: fast for experts, scriptable, low resources, remote use. Points against / limitations: GUI uses more memory/processing and hides advanced options; CLI needs commands to be learned and errors are easy to make. Conclusion: GUI for general staff, CLI for technical administrators.

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Compare a compiler and an interpreter in terms of how errors are reported. (b) Explain why an interpreter is useful when a program is being developed.
items.answer: (a) A compiler reports all errors found after translating the whole program; an interpreter stops at the first error it meets. (b) Errors are reported as soon as the line is reached, so they can be corrected and the program continued immediately; parts of the program can be tested without translating everything.
